reuse.why: The change reuses RSchedule, recurConfigToRSchedule and the existing weekend adjustment helper, while sharing holiday matching and daily-drop predicates.

duplication.why: Holiday matching is centralized, but the drop-versus-move orchestration is repeated across next-date lookup, upcoming dates, range dates and budget calculations.

placement.why: The handler and model changes follow existing layers, although occurrence adjustment policy remains partly embedded in server consumers instead of shared schedules logic.

scope.why: All edits directly support daily skipping, range enumeration or holiday handling.

maintainability.why: The shared predicates help, but maintaining four versions of occurrence adjustment and separate holiday-dependent search bounds makes future rule changes cumbersome.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All affected consumers use the existing recurrence and weekend adjustment helpers; the tree has no unified occurrence transformation abstraction that this change bypasses.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate, server/schedules/app.ts:getUpcomingDates/getDatesInRange and server/budget/schedule-template.ts express the same drop-or-move policy through find, filter/map, loop and local closure forms.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter, getNextDate gains daily-specific filtering and adjustment dispatch, and consumers repeat that dispatch while continuing to call the shared primitives.
